question: Should OpenClaw core own a persistent publisher-feed CLI and shared SQLite consumer, or should publisher following be delivered through an external plugin/ClawHub package using a smaller generic core seam?
rationale: The repository policy prefers optional integration and service workflows outside core when existing plugin or manifest contracts suffice; this PR introduces a durable core CLI, network trust boundary, and state model, so the permanent ownership boundary cannot be selected mechanically.

options.title: Externalize the consumer
options.body: Pause this core PR and move publisher follow/refresh behavior into a ClawHub plugin unless a concrete missing core extension API is identified.

options.title: Sponsor a generic core seam
options.body: Keep a narrowly generic signed-feed and state contract in core, but split publisher-specific workflow and policy into a plugin with explicit upgrade and security proof.

options.title: Adopt the full core workflow
options.body: Accept the CLI and shared-state product surface after maintainers explicitly own its long-term configuration, support, and migration contract.

recommendation.title: Externalize the consumer
recommendation.body: Pause this core PR and move publisher follow/refresh behavior into a ClawHub plugin unless a concrete missing core extension API is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible history across the consolidated publisher-feed stack and can clarify the proposed ownership boundary; broader product sponsorship still needs a repository decision-maker.
